title: Google Business Profile for Real Estate Agents and Builders in India
seoTitle: Google Business Profile for Real Estate Agents in India
excerpt: Google Business Profile for real estate agents and builders: project listings, agent profiles, categories, RERA in posts and the review rules.
imageAlt: Residential apartment towers around a swimming pool and landscaped garden, seen from above in an Indian city

inlineImages.alt: A residential tower under construction wrapped in scaffolding, with a tower crane beside it
inlineImages.caption: A project under construction can't hold its own profile; a staffed sales office can.

inlineImages.alt: A small model house with a red front and a set of house keys on a dark table

faqs.question: Can a builder create a Google Business Profile for each project?
faqs.answer: Only for a project with a staffed sales office. Google lists model homes and for-sale properties as ineligible, but says sales or leasing offices are eligible for verification. A tower under construction or a sample flat with nobody there to meet buyers can't have its own profile.

faqs.question: Should every agent in a brokerage have a separate profile?
faqs.answer: Usually not. Google treats real estate agents as individual practitioners and says a single practitioner working in a branded organisation should share the organisation's profile. One strong firm profile collects all the reviews instead of splitting them across several thin listings.

faqs.question: Which Google Business Profile category should a real estate agent choose?
faqs.answer: Brokers usually pick "Real estate agency" or "Real estate agent", builders "Real estate developer" and advisory firms "Real estate consultant". Choose the one that describes the whole business, and add secondary categories only for real, separate services, as Google asks for as few categories as possible.

faqs.question: Can I put a project name or locality in my business name?
faqs.answer: No. Google says your name should reflect your real-world business name and that location details, taglines and other unnecessary information aren't permitted. Use the name on your signboard and RERA registration, and mention projects and localities in posts, services and the description.

faqs.question: Should a channel partner working from home show an address?
faqs.answer: No. If buyers don't visit you, hide the address and set service areas instead. Google allows up to 20 service areas and says the overall area should be no more than about two hours of driving time from where the business is based.

faqs.question: Do Google Business Profile posts need a RERA number?
faqs.answer: Treat project posts as advertisements. The RERA Act says a promoter's advertisement must prominently show the project's registration number and the Authority's website, so include both in every post that promotes a project, and don't post unregistered projects at all.

faqs.question: Can I write my phone number in a Google post?
faqs.answer: It's safer not to. Google's content policy says posts with unverified contact details, including phone numbers, may be removed. Add a Call now button instead, which uses the verified number on your profile, and link the post to the matching project page.

faqs.question: Can channel partners or employees review our real estate firm?
faqs.answer: No. Google's Maps policy bans reviews based on a conflict of interest, including current or former employees and anyone in a contractual relationship with the business. Ask genuine buyers, sellers and tenants instead, and never offer a brokerage discount or gift for a review.

faqs.question: Can buyers chat with me through my Google profile?
faqs.answer: Not through Google's own chat, which ended on 31 July 2024. Buyers can call the number on your profile, and eligible profiles can let customers reach the business by text or WhatsApp. Whichever channel you use, reply quickly and route each enquiry to the right person.
